issues.passage: The committee treated the unfinished draft as the apotheosis of a project still lacking direction.
issues.why: Apotheosis is used correctly as 'ideal / culminating example': the committee regarded the draft as the perfect specimen of a directionless project. Poor judgment does not make the vocabulary wrong.

fix.correctPassage: Critics hailed the final movement as the apotheosis of the composer's lifelong work with form.
wrongPassages: After years of decline, the firm reached its apotheosis when sales hit their lowest recorded level.
She called the first day of training the apotheosis of a career that had not yet produced any finished work.
Historians placed the movement's apotheosis at the moment it dissolved with no public following or achievements.

issues.passage: Historians dated the apotheosis of the movement to the decade before it had any public influence.
issues.why: Apotheosis correctly means the peak or culminating point; dating that peak early is a historical claim, not a misuse of the word.
